items.title: Amgen Stock And The Price Of A Promise
items.summary: Management raised its full-year forecast, but the market seems to be asking for more than a higher target.

items.title: Johnson & Johnson vs AbbVie: Safe Dividend vs Higher Yield
items.summary: Two healthcare giants, two very different dividend bets: one built on six decades of unbroken raises and a fortress balance sheet, the other dangling a fatter yield while racing to outrun its own blockbuster's collapse. Knowing which risk you are actually buying changes everything.

items.title: Two Years Of Growth Barely Change What You Pay For Intuitive Surgical
items.summary: Consensus growth takes only a modest slice off the multiple, and the company has not yet set the instrument pricing that lands inside those two years.

items.title: The Energy and Pharma Giants Quietly Funding HDV’s 3% Yield, and How Safe Each One Is
items.summary: Four dividend giants from energy and pharma quietly generate the bulk of HDV's income, but their balance sheets and payout coverage look nothing alike. Before trusting that 3% yield, it pays to know which checks are ironclad and which carry a hidden catch.

items.title: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) Advances Seltorexant And Expands Outpatient Cardiac Care
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) is advancing its novel antidepressant Seltorexant into late stage clinical development for major depressive disorder as a potential rapid acting treatment option. The company also entered a multi year partnership with ACCESS to expand adoption of advanced cardiac electrophysiology technologies in ambulatory surgery centers. Both moves align with Johnson & Johnson’s focus on higher growth therapeutic and medtech areas that are important for its long term...

items.title: Intuitive Surgical: Oppenheimer now bullish, sees competition being "crowded out"
items.summary: Investing.com -- Oppenheimer upgraded Intuitive Surgical to Outperform from Perform with a $500 price target in a note on Wednesday, arguing the company's strategy of "Crowding Out Competitors" is strategically smart.

items.title: Why Revolution Medicines May Be Big Pharma’s Next Takeover Target
items.summary: RAS mutations fuel nearly a third of all cancers, and one biotech has quietly built the deepest late-stage pipeline targeting them. Now the biggest names in pharma are circling, and the math on who can actually write the check gets complicated fast.
